title: to in at (places 3)
subtitle: go to work / be at work
summary: Use to for the place you go, and in or at for the place where you are; go home and get home take no preposition.

lesson.heading: to = where you go
lesson.text: After verbs of movement (**go**, **come**, **return**, **walk**, **drive**) we use **to** + the place.

examples.text: I want to **go to Italy** next year.
We walked from my house **to the centre of town**.
What time do you **go to bed**?

lesson.heading: in and at = where you are
lesson.text: After **be**, **stay**, **live** and *do something* we use **in** or **at** + the place. Nobody is moving here.

left.label: to (you go there)
examples: The bus is going **to the airport**.
I went **to a party** last night.

right.label: in / at (you are there)
examples: I met a lot of people **at the party**.

lesson.heading: home
lesson.text: With **home** we use no preposition after go, come, walk or get. But for the place we say **at home**.

examples.text: Dan doesn't go to an office. He **works at home**.

lesson.heading: arrive and get
lesson.text: We **arrive in** a country or a town, but we **arrive at** other places. With **get** we always say **get to**.

examples.text: What time did you **arrive at the hotel**?
What time did you **get to** the hotel?
What time did you **get to** Paris?
I was tired when I **got home**.
examples.note: or: when I arrived home - no preposition

lesson.text: Never say ~~to home~~: it is *I'm going home* and *I'm at home*.

exercises.explanation: go + to + the place you travel to.

exercises.prompt: Sue is on holiday ___ Italy at the moment.
exercises.explanation: She is there now, so we use in.

exercises.prompt: I was tired, so I stayed ___ bed late.
exercises.explanation: stay + in bed: this is where she was.

exercises.prompt: What time do you usually go ___ bed?
exercises.explanation: go to bed is movement, so we use to.

exercises.prompt: Tina is not very well. She has gone ___ the doctor.
exercises.explanation: go / has gone + to + the place.

exercises.prompt: There were 20,000 people ___ the football match.
exercises.explanation: The people were there, so we use at.

exercises.prompt: Do we say arrive in or arrive at with each place?
After the accident three people were taken ___ hospital.
exercises.explanation: They were moved there, so we use to.

exercises.statement: They arrived to England last week.
exercises.explanation: They arrived in England last week. We say arrive in a country or a town.

exercises.statement: What time did you arrive at the hotel?
exercises.explanation: We say arrive at for places like a hotel, a station or work.

exercises.prompt: You ate in a restaurant and then returned to your hotel. Put the sentence in order.
exercises.answer: We had a good meal at a restaurant, and then we went back to the hotel.
exercises.explanation: at a restaurant (where you were) but back to the hotel (where you went).
